subject: Future Tech
title: JET: Europe's Record Holder
description: A 60-second lesson on JET: Europe's Record Holder.

hook.text: In 2022, JET in England set a fusion energy record: 59 megajoules in 5 seconds. Then it shut down forever.

buildup.text: JET operated since 1983 as the world's largest tokamak. It was the testbed for everything ITER would attempt at scale.

discovery.text: JET used deuterium-tritium fuel—the actual mix future reactors will use. Most other machines use deuterium only.

twist.text: JET's final run proved that plasma can be controlled for meaningful durations. The data will guide ITER for decades.

climax.text: After 40 years and 100,000 experiments, JET retired in 2023. Its legacy lives on in every fusion machine that follows.

punchline.text: 40 years of data, one sunset, and a road map for the future.

quiz.question: What record did JET set in its final experiments?
options: 59 megajoules of fusion energy in 5 seconds
